questions.prompt: According to the lecturer, why do information campaigns alone rarely produce lasting behavioral change?
options: People generally distrust statistics published by public agencies.
High awareness does not automatically overcome the friction of daily routines.
Most campaigns focus too heavily on financial penalties rather than rewards.
Media coverage tends to fade before citizens understand the core message.

questions.prompt: What did the cafeteria study demonstrate about changing the default option?
options: Diners complained when low-carbon meals were listed at the top of the menu.
Price discounts were twice as effective as changing menu layout.
Placing plant-based dishes as the standard daily special increased their selection without restricting choice.
Calorie labels had a stronger effect on staff than on students.

questions.prompt: What caution does the lecturer raise at the end of the talk?

Laboratory experiments on habit formation cannot be replicated in workplaces.
Digital reminders always cause fatigue within the first week.
